notes: The source map spreads Tai and Austroasiatic rice farmers over most of China and India; replaced with the regional cultures of c. 2000 BCE.
The Ur III state fell c. 2004 BCE; the map shows its last years.
The Bantu expansion had barely begun c. 2000 BCE.
Sub-Saharan Africa filled with the farming and foraging peoples of the 1500 BCE map.
Named the remaining unclaimed regions after their regional peoples.
Peoples of the deep past are named for their time: early modern humans, the Iberomaurusian and Capsian cultures, foragers before farming and herding spread.
The Caribbean islands were settled from about 5000 BCE (the Bahamas from about 700 CE): Archaic peoples, then the Saladoid peoples and the Taíno.
Mesoamerica is named for its peoples and states of the time.
Early South American cultures are drawn where they lived (lines approximate).
